commit.message:
Verify the DBBI-minus-VIC YOUWON finding with null tests; record as planted marker

dbbi (91 symbols) and the Phase-3.2 VIC plaintext (91 letters) subtracted mod 26 yield
YOUWON in clear, leaving exactly 64 characters - the length of a hex private key. Neither
length was chosen, and three algebraically equivalent parameterisations give the identical
string, so this is one natural rule rather than a fitted one.

Null tests, same rule, over dbbi's own multiset: 0 occurrences of YOUWON in 200,000
shuffles and 0 in 200,000 i.i.d. draws; any 6-letter dictionary word appears in only 0.86%
of shuffles, and the real output contains no dictionary word at all. This is a materially
different class of result from the previously rejected KEY-in-column-sums claim, which had
a free per-cell mask and was forceable in nearly every window of every block.

It is still not key material: the 64-char tail uses 24 distinct letters so it is not hex,
its entropy is flat, and it decrypts nothing (campaign_15_youwon, 2730 trials, all forms
and both rule directions). Recorded as a planted confirmation marker establishing that dbbi
is meant to be operated against the VIC sentence as numbers mod 26.

Declined separately: building a hash-and-check oracle against an asserted third-party
address with no provenance in any primary material.

commit.message:
Close the OP_RETURN script-VM hypothesis on logic

The load-bearing observation - that recursing into the 71-byte payload leaves a push
'exactly one byte short' - is forced rather than suggestive. For a payload of length L whose
first byte is B, the shortfall is B-(L-1); here L=71 and B=ord('G')=71, so L==B and the
shortfall is identically +1 for every such record and can never balance. The coincidence is
that a 71-byte record begins with 'G' and ord('G') is 71, which is a fact about the label.
JH and BH share one format and length, so that is one coincidence observed twice.

The carry bytes proposed to resolve it are inconsistent (0x0d vs 0x4c, each an arbitrary
first byte of a following output amount) and require crossing a script-length boundary that
Bitcoin's encoding forbids. The other cited opcodes are ASCII artifacts of reading English
text as script.

The Bitcoin facts in the source analysis are correct and preserved: no loops, no EVAL,
OP_RETURN halts, nothing self-executes, and the proposed emulator was offline. Also noted:
the authenticated archive excludes OP_RETURN dust on purpose, so these records are not
primary material.

commit.message:
Measure the two claims behind recurring false decrypts

Confirms empirically that the IV is emitted by EVP_BytesToKey rather than chosen, using the
known-good Phase 3.2 decrypt, and records the nuance that makes zero-IV claims look
credible: the correct key with a zero IV still prints about 94% readable text because CBC
corrupts only the first block and self-heals afterwards. The decisive direction is the
converse, since a wrong key gives nothing readable for any IV, so naming an IV specifies no
construction at all.

Measures the padding false-positive rate directly: against the real 80-byte ciphertext,
300,000 random keys produced 1,235 PKCS#7-valid results, one in 243 against a theoretical
one in 256, and zero that also passed this harness's acceptance gate. A hundred-thousand
candidate battery therefore throws roughly 400 padding-valid results by chance, which
explains the steady stream of claimed Cosmic decryptions and validates the pad>=4, magic
prefix or printability rule.

commit.message:
Settle the no-password claim using the OpenSSL file format

A fair objection held that if the blobs were produced with a raw key and IV there would be
no password to find. That is decidable, because the two OpenSSL modes write different
formats. Demonstrated on identical plaintext: password mode prepends the literal ASCII magic
Salted__ plus eight salt bytes, while raw key and IV mode writes no header at all and the
ciphertext begins at byte zero, a 16-byte difference.

All three GSMG locks carry the magic and a salt, so a password provably exists. The salt is
present precisely because the key derivation function consumed it, and that function emits
the key and the IV together, so there is no separate IV input and no key/IV pair standing in
for a password. This also re-confirms the three solved stages under the same convention.

Consequence: the password batteries target the right kind of object. They fail because the
passphrase has not been derived, not because the locks take a key and IV.

Test and close stage chaining from the confirmed dbbi operation

The one confirmed operation is dbbi minus VIC, which plants YOUWON against a 0-in-200k null.

outputs had never been used that way, so this tests faed against all six stage-one derived

commit.message:
Exhaustively close pi as raw AES key and IV material

Runs the proposed pi hypothesis as a superset of the suggested script, which checked about
thirty combinations and accepted on padding alone. Padding alone was previously measured at a
one-in-243 false-positive rate on these ciphertexts, so that criterion would have reported
roughly 2,600 spurious successes across a sweep this size.

Instead: pi computed locally to 1200 digits, both the fractional and full forms, both ASCII
and nibble-packed byte interpretations, every key offset from 0 to 199 crossed with every IV
offset from 0 to 199 rather than only the five proposed, against the P32T ciphertext and
whole file, the cosmic ciphertext and the miniA ciphertext, plus sha256 of pi prefixes at six
lengths. 640,480 direct decrypts and zero hits under the strict gate.

Records two method corrections. Padding-only acceptance is not a success criterion at this
scale. And re-inserting a dummy Salted header to brute-force a password cannot work, because
the salt is an input to the key derivation, so an invented salt derives a different key and
the original plaintext stays unreachable regardless of how many passwords are tried.

commit.message:
Explain why a padding oracle attack cannot apply to the GSMG blobs

Addresses the Telegram proposal to reach the key via an oracle padding attack. It fails for
three independent reasons, any one fatal. There is no oracle, since the attack is interactive
and requires a live service that decrypts chosen ciphertexts under the secret key and leaks a
padding-validity bit per query, whereas GSMG is static files with no endpoint. The attack
recovers plaintext rather than a key, so it cannot produce the SHA-256 key the thread wants.
And it is self-defeating, because asking the oracle whether padding is valid requires
decrypting with the very secret the puzzle withholds, so it would need the secret to attack
the secret.

Records where the confusion arises: padding is a real result of correct decryption but not a
lever to find the key, and random keys produce valid padding one time in 243 as measured
earlier, so padding is not even a search signal. Also notes that Trinity's exploit in Reloaded
was an SSH CRC-32 attack rather than a padding oracle, so the film metaphor does not name this
technique, and that the key-not-password and IV-window claims were already settled by the
Salted header proof and the exhaustive pi and IV closures.

Run preregistered tick 1b: 2x14 board coordinates vs P32T, then park the branch
